title: Observer-driven derate/holdback and transparent fallback protocol for model dependencies
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: When downstream model dependencies degrade (high latency, error spikes, or region outage), we need a predictable, safe way to reduce load on the dependency while keeping customer-facing latency and correctness acceptable. Existing per-tenant circuit policies are binary or coarse-grained and can cause sudden quality regressions or long outages for tenants during transient spikes.

Goal: Implement an 'observer-driven derate and holdback' protocol that: 1) continuously observes SLO burn-rate and smoothed error/latency distributions per dependency/model/tenant, 2) applies graduated derates (rate caps, percent traffic diversion to smaller/quantized variants, and increased caching) instead of full trips, 3) introduces a short 'holdback escrow' window to keep in-flight KV/cache integrity during stateful failovers, and 4) provides transparent fallback to safe alternatives (cached responses, embedding-only paths, or low-cost short models) with annotated responses for downstream clients.

Design summary:
- Observers: per-region and per-tenant observers compute a 60s burn-rate and a 10m decayed percentile series (p50/p90/p99) for latency and p95 error rate. Observers run in the control plane and emit an ordered list of candidate mitigations when thresholds are crossed.
- Derate steps: 1) Soft-rate-limit (e.g., reduce QPS by X% for offending tenant), 2) Model-derate (route Y% to smaller/quantized model variant), 3) Cache-first (check prefix/KV cache and allow cached responses up to T seconds stale), 4) Fallback route (route Z% to pre-approved fallback model or embedding-based stub).
- Holdback escrow: when transitioning cache-backed or stateful handlers, pause write-throughs for 5s while redirecting a small probe traffic sample to the target region/variant to ensure KV compatibility and prevent split-brain.
- Transparent fallback: responses from fallbacks include metadata headers (x-redwood-fallback: true, fallback-reason, fallback-variant) so clients and Console can attribute quality delta.
- Canary rejoin policy: progressive reintroduction uses sampled replays and success probes; full rejoin requires 5m of p95 latency under threshold and successful KV handshake.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end tests simulate a region with 3x latency and validate progressive derate sequence occurs without hard-tripping.
- Console shows per-tenant derate events with annotated metrics and fallback breakdown.
- No dropped writes or KV inconsistency in integration tests with holdback escrow enabled.
- Rollout plan exercised in staging with synthetic traffic and Chaos tests for region failover.

Telemetry and dashboards: Update Grafana composite to include "Derate Incidents" (count, duration, by-tenant/model), fallback type distribution, p95 before/after derate, and consumer-facing error uplift. Add SLO alert rule: if derate duration for a tenant exceeds 10m and customer impact high, page on-call.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag in control plane controlling observer thresholds (staged per region).
2) Internal dogfood for top 10 tenants in staging for 2 weeks.
3) Canary: enable for 5% of production traffic for non-SLA tenants.
4) Full enable for non-SLA tenants and measured enable for SLA tenants after ops review.

Notes on safety:
- Derate is designed to be monotonic (never increase load on a degraded dependency).
- Holdback escrow default window is conservative (5s) but configurable per-dependency.
- All fallback routes require pre-approval lists to avoid unvetted models being used as fallbacks.
